# prism-boundary Specification

<!-- Generated by Prism from prism/spec.json. Change the app through your agent with /prism, not by editing this file. -->

## Purpose

Prism Boundary: Decides whether one labeled fact about the owner may go to a destination, so that nothing moves while the Prism is halted, no personal fact is ever saved to GitHub or the hosted verifier, no personal identifier leaves the browser, and nothing is sent without the owner's signed approval.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Always deny when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `deny` when halted is yes, because when the owner presses the kill switch nothing may move (constitution P7).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-001, theorem `inv001Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-001 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `public none browser none no yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`
- **AND** the app answers `deny`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: Always deny when destination is github

The app SHALL answer `deny` when destination is github, because the owner's personal data must never be saved to GitHub.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-002, theorem `inv002Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-002 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `public none github owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`
- **AND** the app answers `deny`, decided by REQ-002

### Requirement: Always deny when destination is verifier

The app SHALL answer `deny` when destination is verifier, because personal data on the hosted verifier is unlisted but not private.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-003, theorem `inv003Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-003 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `public none verifier owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`
- **AND** the app answers `deny`, decided by REQ-003

### Requirement: Never allow when detector is not none

The app SHALL NOT answer `allow` when detector is not none, because card, health, credential and special-category data must never be stored or moved as a value (PCI DSS 3, HIPAA 164.312, GDPR 9).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-004, theorem `inv004Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-004 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `confidential pci browser none no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `allow`
- **AND** the app answers `hashonly`, decided by REQ-004

### Requirement: Never allow when label is restricted

The app SHALL NOT answer `allow` when label is restricted, because restricted data must never be stored or moved as a value.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-005, theorem `inv005Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-005 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `restricted none browser owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `allow`
- **AND** the app answers `hashonly`, decided by REQ-005

### Requirement: Never allow when destination is outbound and approval is none

The app SHALL NOT answer `allow` when destination is outbound and approval is none, because nothing is ever sent without the owner's OK.

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-006, theorem `inv006Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-006 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `confidential none outbound none no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `allow`
- **AND** the app answers `ask`, decided by the fallback

### Requirement: Never allow when identifier is yes and destination is not browser

The app SHALL NOT answer `allow` when identifier is yes and destination is not browser, because a personal identifier must never leave the browser, even with approval (constitution P5 and the output court).

Verified: to be proved by Lean for every request (INV-007, theorem `inv007Holds`).

#### Scenario: INV-007 holds

- **WHEN** the request is `confidential none outbound owner yes no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL NOT be `allow`
- **AND** the app answers `deny`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: REQ-001 deny when halted is yes

The app SHALL answer `deny` when halted is yes, because stop means stop (kill switch).

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule1`).

#### Scenario: REQ-001 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `public none browser none no yes` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-001

### Requirement: REQ-002 deny when destination is github

The app SHALL answer `deny` when destination is github and no earlier rule matches, because no personal fact is ever saved to GitHub.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule2`).

#### Scenario: REQ-002 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `public none github owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-002

The app SHALL answer `deny` when destination is verifier and no earlier rule matches, because the verifier sees the model only, never facts.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule3`).

#### Scenario: REQ-003 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `public none verifier owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-003

The app SHALL answer `hashonly` when label is restricted and destination is browser and no earlier rule matches, because restricted data is never stored as a value.

#### Scenario: REQ-005 decides

- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `hashonly`, decided by REQ-005

The app SHALL answer `deny` when detector is not none and no earlier rule matches, because regulated data never leaves its source.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule6`).

#### Scenario: REQ-006 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `internal phi outbound owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-006

### Requirement: REQ-007 deny when label is restricted

The app SHALL answer `deny` when label is restricted and no earlier rule matches, because restricted data never leaves its source.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule7`).

#### Scenario: REQ-007 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `restricted none outbound owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-007

### Requirement: REQ-008 deny when identifier is yes and destination is not browser

The app SHALL answer `deny` when identifier is yes and destination is not browser and no earlier rule matches, because no personal identifier leaves the browser (output court).

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule8`).

#### Scenario: REQ-008 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `confidential none outbound owner yes no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-008

### Requirement: REQ-009 allow when destination is browser

The app SHALL answer `allow` when destination is browser and no earlier rule matches, because the encrypted browser store holds labeled facts.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule9`).

#### Scenario: REQ-009 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `public none browser none no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `allow`, decided by REQ-009

### Requirement: REQ-010 allow when approval is owner

The app SHALL answer `allow` when approval is owner and no earlier rule matches, because only the owner may send.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors (`rule10`).

#### Scenario: REQ-010 decides

- **WHEN** the request is `confidential none outbound owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `allow`, decided by REQ-010

### Requirement: Otherwise ask

The app SHALL answer `ask` when no rule matches, because nothing is sent without the owner.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: No rule matches

- **WHEN** the request is `confidential none outbound none no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `ask`

### Requirement: The first matching rule decides

The app SHALL try REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-005, REQ-006, REQ-007, REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010 in that order, and the first rule that matches SHALL decide.

Verified: tested by the acceptance vectors.

#### Scenario: Two rules match

- **WHEN** the request is `public none github owner no no` (an acceptance example)
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `deny`, decided by REQ-002, the earlier rule

### Requirement: Request and answers

The app SHALL read one request as one line of 6 fields separated by single spaces, in this order, and SHALL answer exactly one of `allow`, `hashonly`, `ask`, `deny`, or `invalid` for anything else.

| Field | Accepts | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `public`, `internal`, `confidential`, `restricted`, `unlabeled` | the fact's classification label |
| `detector` | `none`, `pci`, `phi`, `credential`, `special` | which regulated-data detector matched the fact: card data, health data, a credential, or a GDPR special category |
| `destination` | `browser`, `github`, `verifier`, `outbound` | where the fact would go: the encrypted store in the owner's browser, GitHub (the Pages repository, its commits and build output), the hosted verifier, or an outbound message |
| `approval` | `none`, `owner` | whether the owner signed an approval for this move |
| `identifier` | `no`, `yes` | whether the fact is a personal identifier, such as a name, email address, phone number or account number |
| `halted` | `no`, `yes` | whether the owner has pressed the kill switch |

| Answer | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `allow` | the fact may go there |
| `hashonly` | only its hash and a pointer to the original may be kept |
| `ask` | the owner must approve first |
| `deny` | the fact may not go there |
| `invalid` | the request is malformed |

Verified: reading a request is tested, not proved.

#### Scenario: A malformed request is invalid

- **WHEN** the request is not 6 fields in this order
- **THEN** the answer SHALL be `invalid`

## Out of scope

- It does not decide a fact's label or run the detectors; those come from the extractor.
- It does not check the owner's signature; the approval field is set only after the signature verifies.
- The owner's approval cannot release anything to GitHub, nor restricted or detected data anywhere.
- It governs the Prism at run time; a repository check must also refuse any commit that carries personal data.
- Recipient addresses of an approved outbound message are handled by the mail client, not stored as facts.

## Examples

- `public none github owner no no` gives `deny`
- `public none browser none no no` gives `allow`
- `confidential none browser none no no` gives `allow`
- `confidential pci browser none no no` gives `hashonly`
- `restricted none browser owner no no` gives `hashonly`
- `confidential none github none no no` gives `deny`
- `public none verifier owner no no` gives `deny`
- `confidential none outbound none no no` gives `ask`
- `confidential none outbound owner no no` gives `allow`
- `internal phi outbound owner no no` gives `deny`
- `restricted none outbound owner no no` gives `deny`
- `unlabeled none browser none no no` gives `allow`
- `public none browser none no yes` gives `deny`
- `confidential none outbound owner no yes` gives `deny`
- `confidential none outbound owner yes no` gives `deny`
- `confidential none browser none yes no` gives `allow`
- `public none outbound owner yes no` gives `deny`

## What is proved and what is tested

Lean proves each property marked proved above, for every request that decodes, with no exceptions and no sampling. The proof is about `judge`, the function the WebAssembly guest runs, because both come from the same model.

The parsing of requests is tested, not proved: the acceptance vectors in the app replay through the built guest, including malformed and oversized requests.

Nothing here says the rules are the right rules. That is the part only you can judge.
